title: Introducing Claude Meetings
summary: Claude Meetings is a beta in which Claude joins Google Meet video calls as a visible participant on Team and Enterprise plans. Claude can answer questions by voice or chat, build docs and whiteboards live, and write notes and action items, with each meeting saved as a claude.ai page containing notes, transcript, and built artifacts. It stays out of calls with outside guests unless an admin allows it, stores transcripts and summaries rather than audio, and is not available for ZDR, HIPAA-ready, or CMEK orgs during beta.

title: The Claude Tag guide for startups
summary: This guide covers Claude Tag (beta), a Slack-based tool for Team and Enterprise where teams @mention Claude, connect tools, and assign tasks. It profiles eight startups using it for on-call triage, Slack-to-draft-PR, company Q&A, self-serve data, and recurring reports, with results such as Campfire going from mention to PR in 21 minutes and NavigateAI merging 134 PRs. Guardrails include people reviewing and merging draft PRs, admin connector bundles, per-channel settings, and spend limits.

title: Using a "chaos loop" to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requests.
summary: Claude Docs, a collaborative editor where people and Claude sessions edit live, launched September 16, 2026 after Claude ran continuously on a staging cluster for about two weeks, running load tests, reading telemetry, and proposing and deploying fixes under approval gates for risky changes. A copy-on-write fix cut a large document from about 3 GB to 180 MB and lowered the launch capacity estimate from 500+ pods to about 50. The result was 4.6M+ docs, 2B requests, 60 server errors, and 629 production rolls in September with no rollbacks.

title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification.
summary: In a post by Addy Osmani, the Claude Code team says about 90% of its code is written and reviewed by Claude, enabled by verification loops in which agents cheaply generate end-to-end, property, and differential tests. Practices include a verify skill, human escalation after three failed fixes, a 39-item reliability checklist, deletion of flaky tests, and a commit gate set to off, observe, or enforce. A separate grader using a rubric gave up to a 10-point success gain, and human work shifts toward defining "done" and reviewing evidence.

title: Building always-on agents.
summary: This guide covers stateful, proactive agents that sleep most of the time and wake on events, built from five primitives: event inbox, timers, memory, permissions, and outbox. The renewed interest is attributed to better model judgment and cheaper long-horizon intelligence, citing Opus 5.5 at 78% lower cost per solved task than Opus 5 on one coding benchmark. Reliability depends on deduplication, a single active worker, and persistent memory, unattended agents need credential proxies, auto-mode classifiers, and deferred tool calls for approvals, and the advice is to start quiet and earn user attention over time.

title: J. Crew brings its signature approach to styling to life with Claude.
summary: The J.Crew Style Advisor is an AI stylist on JCrew.com, live for U.S. women's and men's shopping, that builds complete outfits from an occasion or a starting item using looks drawn from J.Crew photo shoots. It was built with Claude Code using multiple models: a frontier model for planning, Sonnet for response decisions, and Haiku for fast tasks. Planned next steps include personalization based on past purchases and more markets and product lines.
